deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to Gauss's Göttingen magnetometer experiments for the absolute determination of terrestrial magnetic intensity, the work published as 'Intensitas vis magneticae terrestris ad mensuram absolutam revocata', 1832/33. The previous page has oscillation series of the needle loaded with weights ('Belastung 250—450', '0—700'). The next page continues the bar-A series up to oscillation 1111.

(A) 'Zur Bestimmung der Torsion' (determination of torsion).
- The torsion circle (Torsionskreis, T.K.) at the top of the suspension wire was set to 150°. At 4h34'6" the mirror-scale reading was 576.655.
- It was then set to 270°. At 4h42'57.5" the reading was 605.329.
- So a twist of u = 120° of the wire top moves the scale reading by Δ = 28.674 divisions.
- In Gauss's theory, the equilibrium condition is mT sin v = Θ(u − v), with v the deflection of the needle. Hence Θ/(mT) ≈ v/(u − v).
- Gauss writes the result as 1/707.
- [Mine] This implies v = 120°/708 ≈ 610.2". One scale division would then be ≈ 610.2/28.674 ≈ 21.3" of needle rotation, which is plausible for his apparatus. The scale constant itself is not on the page, so the 1/707 cannot be recomputed from the page alone.
- 'T.K. wieder auf 210°': the circle is returned to the middle position 210°.

(B) Unloaded oscillations ('Ohne Belastung'), trial period T = 20.78 s.
- Passage times t_n are recorded for n = 0..5 and 120..124.
- The second column is the reduced time t_n − n·20.78 s. It gives 4h50'31.25, 31.17, 31.29, 31.41, 31.28, 31.15 for the first group and 31.80, 31.82, 31.89, 31.91, 31.83 for the second.
- [Mine] The mean reduced epoch drifts from ≈31.26 to ≈31.85 s over 120 swings. The corrected period is therefore ≈ 20.78 + 0.59/120 ≈ 20.785 s, before arc and torsion reductions. Those reductions are not done on the page.
- The pairs beside n = 2, 3 and n = 122 are equilibrium (rest) point and arc in scale divisions:
  - n = 2: 591.683 (or 590.683), arc 1072.833
  - n = 3: 592.283, arc 1070.767
  - n = 122: 599.217, arc 742.767
- The rest point drifts by about 7.5 divisions; this is declination variation.
- Logarithmic decrement per oscillation: log10(1072.833/742.767)/120 = 0.001331. Gauss writes 'Decr. log 0,00133', which is correct.

(C) 'Schwingungen des Stabes A in der Sternwarte' (oscillations of bar A in the observatory).
- Clock comparison: chronometer 11h10'0" = Shelton clock 11h32'7", an offset of 22'7".
- Trial period 12.87 s. Reduced times t_n − 12.87·n are:
  - n = 0..4: 2'57.30, 57.33, 57.32, 57.31, 57.26
  - n = 5, 6: arithmetically 57.69 and 57.76
  - n = 7: 57.21
  - n = 104..109: 57.12, 57.15, 57.22, 57.15, 57.12, 57.15
- Swings 5 and 6 are thus ≈0.5 s out of line. Gauss marks them in the margin '−½?' (transcribed '-1?'). He overwrites the reduced values to 57.19 and 57.26: he suspects a half-second (beat) miscount of the chronometer and corrects by −0.5 s.
- Rest point and arc at n = 107, 108: 644.25, arc 859.5; 644.25, arc 856.5.
- [Mine] From n ≈ 3 to n ≈ 106 the reduced epoch falls by ≈0.13 s, so T ≈ 12.8687 s over this stretch. The next page carries the series to 1111 swings with decrement 0.00117. Check: log10(859.5/58.20)/997 = 0.001173.

Purpose: periods of the unloaded and loaded needle give the moment of inertia, and from it the product mT. The torsion ratio corrects mT for wire torsion. Bar A's period in the observatory feeds the intensity comparison.
errors: No arithmetic errors found in the reduced-time columns: all 26 entries check to 0.01 s, using the half-second-corrected values at n = 5, 6 of bar A.

Bar A, swings 5 and 6: the recorded times 4'2.04 and 4'14.98 give reduced values 57.69 and 57.76, ≈0.5 s off the trend. Gauss himself flags this ('−½?') and corrects the reduced values to 57.19 and 57.26. This is a likely observational miscount of a half-second beat, which he caught.
The value 1/707 cannot be verified from the page alone; it requires the scale-distance constant (≈21.3"/division if 1/707 is correct).

results.what: Determination of the torsion coefficient of the suspension wire relative to the magnetic directive force: twist the torsion circle by 120°, measure the needle deflection, ratio Θ/(mT) = 1/707.
results.modern_name: Torsion correction / torsion ratio of a unifilar magnetometer suspension

results.what: Reduction of passage times t_n − nT0 to obtain a refined period from widely separated groups of swings.
results.modern_name: Method of reduced transit epochs (least-squares-like period determination)

results.what: Logarithmic decrement of amplitude per oscillation from arcs at two epochs: 0.00133 (unloaded needle), 0.00117 (bar A).
results.usually_credited_to: Standard; used systematically by Gauss and Weber

results.what: Oscillation series of bar A in the observatory, with clock comparison between chronometer and Shelton pendulum clock.
results.modern_name: Period measurement for absolute geomagnetic intensity

deep.surprise_reason: Raw laboratory data and routine reductions from Gauss's well-documented 1832–33 absolute-intensity experiments; the methods are exactly those he published in Intensitas.

checkable.asserts: The torsion twist of 120° produced a scale shift of 28.674 divisions.
If Θ/(mT) = 1/707, one scale division ≈ 21.28 arcseconds (consistency check of the scale constant).
Log decrement of the unloaded needle over 120 swings equals 0.00133.
Log decrement of bar A (swing 107 to 1104, next page) equals 0.00117.
Reduced time for n=3 (unloaded) is 31.41 s, not 31.21 or 31.24 (result ≈ 0).
Reduced time for n=104 of bar A is 11h2'57.12 (result ≈ 0).
Raw reduction for bar A n=5 gives 57.69, i.e. 0.5 s off the trend, justifying Gauss's −½ correction (result ≈ 0).
Raw reduction for bar A n=6 gives 57.76; corrected by −0.5 to 57.26 (result ≈ 0).
Refined unloaded period ≈ 20.7849 s from the drift of reduced epochs.

transcription_corrections: Unloaded series, n=3: the reduced value is 31.41 (computed 51'33.75 − 62.34 s = 50'31.41), not 31.21 or 31.24.
Unloaded series, n=4 and n=5: the reduced values are 31.28 and 31.15 (confirmed arithmetically).
Bar A, margin marks at n=5, 6 read '−½?' rather than '-1?'. They indicate a suspected half-second error: the raw reductions 57.69 and 57.76 are overwritten as 57.19 and 57.26.
Bar A, n=5 time: 4'2.04 (final digit 4 overwritten), consistent with raw reduced 57.69.
The first rest point at n=2 is 591.683 or 590.683 (overwritten); it cannot be confirmed without the turning-point readings.
'T. K.' = Torsionskreis (torsion circle); 'Decr. log' = logarithmic decrement; 'Shelton' = the observatory's Shelton pendulum clock.
